title: How to Clean Up Your C Drive on Windows 11 (Fast)
hook: Is your C drive almost full, and Windows keeps nagging you about low disk space? In the next few minutes you'll clear gigabytes of junk with seven safe steps, using only the tools already built into Windows 11, and what to do if space still runs short.
intro: Over time, Windows 11 piles up temporary files, old update leftovers, forgotten downloads and apps you never open. None of this cleanup needs special software or any risky tricks. Everything we'll do is built into Windows, so you can't break anything, and most people recover somewhere between five and fifty gigabytes in about ten minutes. Let's go step by step, starting with the simplest wins first. So grab a coffee, and let's get your PC breathing again.
youNeed: An external drive or cloud storage
youNeedNarration: Here's what you need. A PC running Windows 11, about ten minutes of your time, and an external drive or cloud storage if you want to move large files somewhere safe. You may also need your administrator password for one of the steps. Nothing to buy and nothing to download.
heroImagePrompt: A modern laptop on a clean white desk showing a Windows 11 desktop with a storage settings window open, soft daylight, shallow depth of field, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: See what is eating your space
steps.narration: Step one. Open Settings, choose System, then Storage. Windows shows a colored bar that breaks your C drive into apps, temporary files, documents and other categories, and it can take a minute to finish calculating. Click Show more categories if you see that option. This matters because you should clean the biggest category first instead of guessing. If apps and games take most of the room, step four will help most. If temporary files dominate, the next two steps will give you a quick win. Note your free space now, so you can compare at the end. Don't worry if some numbers look surprising, because hidden folders and caches are often larger than people expect.
steps.imagePrompt: A person's hands on a laptop keyboard while the screen shows a Windows storage usage bar broken into colored categories, bright home office, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Delete temporary files
steps.narration: Step two. Still in Storage, click Temporary files. Windows lists items such as thumbnails, delivery optimization files and the Recycle Bin, with a size next to each one. Tick the boxes for the categories you don't need, and leave Downloads unticked, because that is your personal folder and we'll review it by hand later. Then click Remove files. Windows rebuilds these caches automatically when it needs them, so nothing important is lost. On a PC that has never been cleaned, this single step often frees several gigabytes. It only takes a couple of minutes, so it is a great place to start. Come back to this page every few months.
steps.imagePrompt: A laptop screen showing a checklist of temporary file categories with a green button, clean desk, soft natural light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Run Disk Cleanup for system files
steps.narration: Step three. Type Disk Cleanup into the Start menu and open it, then choose your C drive. Click Clean up system files, which may ask for your administrator password. After a short scan you'll see extra categories, such as Windows Update Cleanup and previous Windows installations. These can be several gigabytes each. Read the descriptions, tick what you no longer need, and click OK. If you installed a big Windows update in the last ten days, keep the previous installation, in case you want to roll back. The scan can take a minute or two, so be patient and keep the window open until it finishes.
steps.tip: Windows Update Cleanup is often huge
steps.mistake: Deleting a recent previous Windows version
steps.imagePrompt: A computer monitor on a desk showing a disk cleanup dialog with a list of file types and checkboxes, calm office, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Uninstall apps you never use
steps.narration: Step four. Go to Settings, Apps, then Installed apps, and sort the list by size. Scroll through it and ask yourself one question for each entry: have I used this in the last six months? Old games, trial software, and duplicate video editors are the usual heavy hitters. Click the three dots next to an app and choose Uninstall. Keep anything made by Microsoft or your computer maker if you are unsure what it does, such as drivers. You can always reinstall a program later, but you cannot easily get back the space. Take your time on this one, since it is where most people recover the most room, especially if there are games on the list.
steps.tip: Sort apps by size, biggest first
steps.imagePrompt: A laptop screen with a list of installed apps sorted by size, a hand holding a mouse, bright modern workspace, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Empty Downloads and the Recycle Bin
steps.narration: Step five. Open File Explorer and click on the Downloads folder. Sort by size, and delete installers and old files you don't recognize. Files you want to keep can be moved elsewhere in the next step. Deleting a file only sends it to the Recycle Bin, so right-click the Recycle Bin on your desktop and choose Empty Recycle Bin to really free the space. Many people forget this, and wonder why the numbers do not change. Take a minute to look at the Desktop and Documents folders as well. It is a small habit, and it keeps clutter from piling up again later.
steps.tip: Sort by size to find giants fast
steps.mistake: Forgetting to empty the Recycle Bin
steps.imagePrompt: A file explorer window showing a downloads folder sorted by file size, large files at the top, on a laptop on a wooden desk, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Move big files off the C drive
steps.narration: Step six. Photos, videos and big projects are the main reason a drive fills up. Plug in an external drive and move them there with cut and paste. Or use OneDrive: right-click a folder in OneDrive and choose Free up space, so the files stay in the cloud and only download when you open them. Either way, you keep your files while giving Windows back the room it needs to run smoothly. Aim to keep at least fifteen percent of the drive free, because Windows slows down when it is nearly full. Check that the files open properly from their new place before you delete the originals, just to be safe.
steps.tip: Keep 15 percent of the drive free
steps.mistake: Moving files without a backup copy
steps.imagePrompt: An external hard drive connected to a laptop with a folder of photos being transferred, tidy desk, soft daylight, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Turn on Storage Sense
steps.narration: Step seven. Go back to Settings, System, Storage, and switch on Storage Sense. Open its settings and choose how often it should run, for example every month, then decide when it empties the Recycle Bin and old files in your Downloads folder. Be careful with the Downloads option, and leave it set to Never unless you are sure. From now on Windows will do the routine cleanup quietly in the background. Finish by checking your free space again, and enjoy the difference you just made. Once it is on, you will rarely need to repeat this whole routine, because the system handles most of it for you.
steps.tip: Set it to run every month
steps.imagePrompt: A laptop screen showing a Windows settings page with a toggle switched on, minimalist desk, soft light, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: STILL STUCK?
bonus.title: If the space will not come back
bonus.narration: Still short on space after all seven steps? Open the Storage page again and look at the biggest category. Check the folders where your phone or camera backs up photos, since those copies quietly fill a drive. Move very large videos to an external drive. Leave unfamiliar system files alone unless you know exactly what they do.
bonus.imagePrompt: A laptop on a tidy desk showing a plain storage settings screen with a colored bar that is almost full, a hand resting on the trackpad, no readable text on screen. Photorealistic photograph for a how-to video. Bright natural light, clean and uncluttered. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: GO FURTHER
bonus.title: When the drive is simply too small
bonus.narration: If you keep running out of room, the drive itself may be too small. Many desktops, and some laptops, accept a second or larger internal drive. For photos and videos, an external drive is the simplest option. Back up your files before any upgrade, and ask a technician if you are unsure about opening the case.
bonus.imagePrompt: A slim external hard drive connected by a cable to a laptop on a wooden desk, a small plant beside it, seen from a three-quarter angle. Photorealistic photograph for a how-to video. Bright natural light, clean and uncluttered. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: KEEP IT CLEAN
bonus.title: Keep the space free
bonus.narration: Set a reminder to check your free space every few months. Look through the Downloads folder once a month, because installers pile up there. Uninstall a program as soon as you stop using it. Keep new photos and videos on an external drive or in the cloud from the start.
bonus.tip: Check free space every few months
bonus.imagePrompt: A desk calendar with a circled date next to an open laptop and a cup of coffee, morning light through a window. Photorealistic photograph for a how-to video. Bright natural light, clean and uncluttered. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Now, the mistakes to avoid. First, never delete files from the Windows or Program Files folders by hand. Windows needs them, and removing them can stop your PC from starting. Second, skip those free registry cleaners and so-called PC boosters. They promise miracles and often cause more problems than they solve. And third, don't clear the Recycle Bin before checking what's inside, because after that, a deleted file is very hard to recover. Take it slowly, and ask yourself before every deletion: do I know what this is?
items: Deleting Windows system folders by hand
Emptying the Recycle Bin without checking

recap.narration: Let's run through it once more. Check what's using your space. Delete temporary files. Run Disk Cleanup for system files. Uninstall apps you don't use. Empty Downloads and the Recycle Bin. Move big files to an external drive or the cloud. And switch on Storage Sense so Windows keeps tidy by itself. Seven steps, ten minutes, and a much faster PC. Then check the bonus sections if space still runs short.

Move big files off the C drive

outro: That's how you clean up your C drive on Windows 11. If this freed up space on your PC, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments how many gigabytes you recovered, and what you would like us to explain next. See you tomorrow.

metadata.title: How to Clean Up Your C Drive on Windows 11 (Fast)
metadata.description:
Is your C drive full? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to clean up your C drive on Windows 11 and free up space fast, using only built-in tools: Settings, Storage, Disk Cleanup and Storage Sense. We remove temporary files, old update leftovers and unused apps, clear Downloads, and move big files to the cloud or an external drive. No registry tricks and no risky software.

You'll need: a pc running windows 11, about ten minutes, an external drive or cloud storage, your windows admin password.
